source_text: Τῷ τιμιωτάτῳ ἀδελφῷ καὶ ὁμοψύχῳ Ἀλεξάνδρῳ Ἀλέξανδρος ὲν Κυρίῳ χαίρειν. Ἡ φίλαρχος τῶν μοχθηρῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ φιλάργυρος πρόθεσις ταῖς δοκούσαις ἀεὶ μείζοσι παροικίαις πέφυκεν ἐπιβουλεύειν, διὰ ποικίλων προφάσεων τῶν τοιούτων ἐπιτιθεμένων τῇ ἐκκλησιαστικῇ εὐσιβείᾳ. Οἰστρηλατούμενοι γὰρ ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐνεργοῦντος ὲν αὐτοῖς διαβόλου εἰς τὴν προκειμένην αὐτοῖς ἡδονὴν, πάσης εὐλαβείας ἀποσκιρτήσαντες, πατοῦσι τὸν τῆς κρίσεως τοῦ Θεοῦ φόβον. Περὶ ὧν ἀναγκαῖον. ἦν μοι τῷ πάσχοντι δηλῶσαι τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ εὐλαβείᾳ, ἵνα φυλάττησθε τοὺς τοιούτους, μή τις αὐτῶν τολμήσῃ καὶ ταῖς ὑμετέραις παροικίαις ἐπιβῆναι, ἤτοι δἰ ἑαυτῶν ʽἱκανοὶ γὰρ ὑποκρίνασθαι πρὸς ἀπάτην οἱ γόητεσ̓, ἣ διὰ γραμμάτων ψευδῶς κεκομψευμένων, καὶ δυναμένων ὑφαρπάσαι τὸν ἁπλῇ πίστει καὶ ἀκεραίῳ προσεσχηκότα. Ἄρειος γοῦν καὶ Ἀχιλλᾶς συνωμοσίαν ἔναγχος ποιησάμενοι, τὴν Κολλούθου φιλαρχίαν πολὺ χεῖρον ἣ ἐκεῖνος ἐζήλωσαν. Ὁ μὲν γὰρ αὐτοῖς τούτοις ἐγκαλῶν, τῆς ἑαυτοῦ μοχθηρᾶς προαιρέσεως εὗρε πρόφασιν. Οἱ δὲ τὴν ἐκείνου Χριστεμπορίαν θεωροῦντες, οὐκ ἔτι τῆς Ἐκκλησίας ὑποχείριοι μένειν ἐκαρτέρησαν: ἀλλ’ ἑαυτοῖς σπήλαια λῃστῶν οἰκοδομήσαντες, ἀδιαλείπτως ἐν αὐτοῖς ποιοῦνται συνόδους, νύκτωρ τε καὶ μεθ̓ ἡμέραν ὲν ταῖς κατὰ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡμῶν διαβολαῖς ἀσκούμενοι. Οἴ πάσης τῆς εὐσεβοῦς ἀποστολικῆς δόξης κατηγοροῦντες, Ἰουδαϊκῷ προσχήματι Χριστομάχον συνεκρότησαν ἐργαστήριον, τὴν θεότητα τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν ἀρνούμενοι, καὶ τοῖς πᾶσιν ἴσον εἷναι κηρύσσοντες. Πᾶσαν τε αὐτοῦ τῆς σωτηρίου οἰκονομίας καὶ δἰ ἡμᾶς ταπεινώσεως φωνὴν ἐκλεξάμενοι, ἐξ αὐτῶν συναγείρειν πειρῶνται τῆς ἀσεβείας ἑαυτῶν τὸ κήρυγμα, τῆς ἀρχῆθεν θεότητος αὐτοῦ, καὶ παρὰ τῷ Πατρὶ δόξης ἀλέκτου τοὺς λόγους ἀποστρεφόμενοι. Τὴν γοῦν Ἑλλήνων τε καὶ Ἰουδαίων ἀσεβῆ περὶ Χριστοῦ δόξαν κρατύνοντες, τὸν παῤ αὐτῶν ἔπαινον ὡς ἔνι μάλιστα θηρῶνται, πάντα μὲν ὅσα καθ̓ ἡμῶν παῤ αὐτοῖς γελᾶται πραγματευόμενοι, στάσεις δὲ ἡμῖν καθ̓ ἡμέραν καὶ διωγμοὸς ἐπεγείροντες: καὶ τοῦτο μὲν δικαστήρια συγκροτοῦντες δἰ ἐντυχίας γυναικαρίων ἀτάκτων ⟨?⟩ ἠπάτησαν: τοῦτο δὲ τὸν Χριστιανισμὸν διασύροντες ἐκ τοῦ περιτροχάζειν πᾶσαν ἀγυιὰν ἀσέμνως τὰς παῤ αὐτοῖς νεωτέρας. Ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν ἄῤῥηκτον τοῦ Χριστοῦ χιτῶνα, ὃν οἱ δήμιοι διελεῖν οὐκ ἐβουλεύσαντο, αὐτοὶ σχίσαι ἐτόλμησαν.
pass_a_gloss: To the most honored brother and like-minded Alexander, Alexander in the Lord greets. The love of power of wicked people and love of money intention has been accustomed to plot against the seemingly greater residences, through various pretexts of such people being imposed on the ecclesiastical piety. For being goaded by the devil working in them into the pleasure presented to them, having cast away all reverence, they trample on the fear of God's judgment. It was necessary for me, suffering, to declare to your reverence, so that you may guard against such people, lest any of them dare to also invade your residences, either through themselves (for the impostors are sufficient to answer with deceit), or through letters falsely composed, and able to snatch away the one who has approached with simple faith and unmixed. For Arius and Achilles, having recently made a conspiracy, emulated the love of power of Colluthus much worse than he did. For he, accusing them, found a pretext for his own wicked choice. But they, observing his Christ-mastery, did not endure to remain subject to the Church; but having built dens of robbers for themselves, they continually hold meetings in them, day and night, practicing in the slanders against Christ and us. They, accusing all the pious apostolic glory, with a Jewish pretense, established a workshop of Christ-fighting, denying the divinity of our Savior, and preaching that all are equal. Having chosen all the voice of his saving economy and through us humiliation, they try to gather from them the proclamation of their impiety, of his divinity from the beginning, and turning away the words unsearchable from the Father. For they, strengthening the impious glory of the Greeks and Jews concerning Christ, hunt for praise from them as much as possible, managing all the things laughed at by them against us, and raising up daily stases and persecutions against us; and this, gathering courts through chance encounters with disorderly women, they deceived; and this, reviling Christianity, from turning every street shamelessly, their newer ways. But they also dared to tear the seamless tunic of Christ, which the soldiers did not plan to divide.

choices.why: νεωτέρας refers to new things/innovations, not younger women
προσεσχηκότα is a participle meaning having approached/received, not unmixed intention

pass_b_english: To my most honored brother and kindred spirit Alexander, Alexander sends greetings in the Lord. A lust for power among the wicked, joined with a greedy purpose, has long been in the habit of plotting against the seemingly larger congregations, using various pretexts that such men impose upon the Church's piety. Driven by the devil working in them toward the pleasure set before them, they have thrown off all reverence and trample the fear of God's judgment. Because I am suffering, I found it necessary to declare this to your reverence, so that you may guard against such people, lest any of them dare to invade your congregations as well — whether through themselves, for the impostors are well able to answer with deceit, or through falsely composed letters capable of snatching away the one who has approached with simple faith and a pure heart.

Arius and Achilles, having recently formed a conspiracy, have outdone even Colluthus in their lust for power. Colluthus, while accusing them, merely found a pretext for his own wicked choice. But they, seeing his trafficking in Christ, could no longer endure to remain subject to the Church; instead, they built dens of robbers for themselves and hold meetings there continually, day and night, practicing slanders against Christ and against us. They accuse the whole pious apostolic glory and, under a Jewish pretense, have established a workshop for fighting against Christ, denying the divinity of our Savior and preaching that all beings are equal. Selecting every utterance of his saving economy and of his humiliation for our sake, they try to assemble from these the proclamation of their own impiety — turning away from his divinity from the beginning and the unsearchable words that belong to the Father. Embracing the impious view of both Greeks and Jews concerning Christ, they hunt for praise from them as eagerly as possible, managing all the things laughed at by them against us, and stirring up daily factions and persecutions against us. On one occasion they convened courts through chance encounters with disorderly women and deceived them; on another, they dragged Christianity through every street, shamelessly parading their newer innovations. They even dared to tear the seamless tunic of Christ, which the soldiers did not plan to divide.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex syntax of the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The translator correctly identified 'νεωτέρας' as innovations/new ways rather than younger women, and correctly translated 'προσεσχηκότα' as having approached/received. The distinction between the 'Christ-mastery' (Χριστεμπορίαν) and the 'workshop of Christ-fighting' (Χριστομάχον ἐργαστήριον) is preserved.

The Greek text is correctly identified as Ep. 1 from Theodoret, HE, and the translation accurately reflects the content. The title 'Warning Against the Arian Heresy' appropriately captures the thought of the text. No OCR damage or uncertain readings are noted.
